claims.text: Atomic dispersion of Pt within a Cu matrix creates isolated Pt active sites.
Isolated Pt sites in Pt/Cu weaken propylene adsorption relative to monometallic Pt.
Pt site isolation disrupts adsorption-energy scaling relationships characteristic of monometallic Pt.
Weaker propylene adsorption causes more rapid propylene desorption.
Rapid propylene desorption suppresses subsequent dehydrogenation and increases propylene selectivity.
The Cu matrix modifies the electronic and ligand environment of isolated Pt atoms.
Incipient-wetness impregnation at a high Cu-to-Pt ratio followed by controlled heat treatment will anchor Pt as isolated sites on Cu nanoparticles.
Contiguous Pt ensembles on monometallic Pt bind propylene more strongly than isolated Pt sites in Pt/Cu.
Stronger propylene adsorption on contiguous Pt ensembles promotes further dehydrogenation.
At approximately 520 °C and atmospheric pressure, Pt/Cu SAA catalysts will have significantly higher propylene selectivity than monometallic Pt catalysts.
Propylene selectivity over the Pt/Cu SAA catalyst will approach approximately 90%.
High-resolution TEM and XPS can establish atomic Pt dispersion and rule out Pt clustering or ensemble formation.
The proposed effect should hold around 520 °C when the support does not independently alter the reaction pathway.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant propylene-selectivity enhancement relative to monometallic Pt is a falsifying outcome.
Observation of significant Pt clustering is designated as a falsifying outcome.
